integrity: Exact full proof provided with a standalone checker for finite small-graph and rational factorization tests; finite checks do not establish the infinite statement. Source comparison has access limits; no independent audit.
scientific_limitations: The sign law applies only when a tree component is feasible. The macroscopic cutoff concerns the minimum feasible edge count and does not imply a positive probability of large tree components. The 1990 Pittel full text was inaccessible; historical priority and whether its proof implicitly contains this finite law remain unresolved. The public 2013 lecture notes visibly bear the date November 26, 2013; first web posting was not independently verified.
title: A one-crossing covariance law for isolated vertices and tree components in fixed-edge random graphs
